en.title: Fewest Distinct Distribution Centers Matching Adjacent Demand Trends
en.description:
On day i, choose a center numbered 1..n. If demand is higher than on the previous day, the center number must be strictly higher; if demand is lower, it must be strictly lower; if demand is equal, the same center must be used. Minimize the number of distinct centers used over all days.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains each day's demand. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, 0≤demand≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 3 and 1. Equal demands do not interrupt a continuing rising constraint.
hints: Ignore consecutive equal demands, find the maximum number of comparisons in a run that is strictly rising or strictly falling, and add 1.
